results.title: Captured domain logo is shown on every brand surface of the app

steps.title: Given analysis A1 exists with a captured domain
steps.expected: A1 is listed in the analyses list

steps.title: When the user opens the report list
steps.expected: The A1 row shows logo L1

steps.title: And the user opens the Overview of A1
steps.expected: The dashboard sidebar and header show logo L1

steps.title: Then the target brand row of the brand rankings in Overview shows logo L1
steps.expected: Logo L1, not the favicon of a domain cited by the AI answers

steps.title: When the user opens a Category view
steps.expected: The target brand row of the rankings shows logo L1

steps.title: And the user opens a competitive view
steps.expected: The target brand shows logo L1
steps.data: e.g. the competitor comparison of A1

results.notes: Observed (Nike): report list row img = google favicon nike.com sz=64 (L1); dashboard sidebar/header brand block "Nike logo" = L1 (the brand header is the sidebar block; no separate header logo exists); Overview brand rankings target row (data-testid dashboard-rankings-row-Nike, highlighted) = L1; Category view "Running Shoes" rankings target row = L1; competitive view: the Competitive prompts of the prompts table won by Nike show L1 in the winner cell (Brand Prioritization matrix and Share of Voice show no brand logos at all, there is no other competitor comparison page). For Nike the AI-cited domain is also nike.com, so the "not the favicon of a cited domain" clause is not discriminating on Nike; it is proven on Decathlon: API brand-rankings gives the target row domain decathlon.com.dz (Overview) and decathlon.co.uk (Category Sporting Goods), while the UI target row shows the decathlon.com favicon (stored domain) on both. Same logo source on every surface (Google favicon of the stored domain). | Test data substitution (user decision 2026-10-23): A1 "Licter" + licter.com could not be created (prompt pool 996/1000), so the TC was replayed on existing ranked staging analyses: Nike cce7a7dc (primary, stored entityDomain nike.com, entityDomainConfirmed=true) and Decathlon b6c8b664 (second check, stored entityDomain decathlon.com, entityDomainConfirmed=true). "The captured domain" = the stored domain; L1 = the logo the app serves for it. Both brands are Brandfetch suggestions, not custom brands with a typed website (per P1 a captured website behaves like a selected suggestion), so the custom-brand path itself is still to be confirmed on A1. Logo source: the stored entityLogoUrl (cdn.brandfetch.io icon) answers HTTP 410 Gone in the browser, so the app falls back to the Google favicon of the stored domain (https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=nike.com&sz=64), which is L1 on every surface checked.
